messages:
lucy: heads up — since ~02:03 UTC we're seeing a sustained NVMe IOPS spike in ap-southeast1 that coincides with GPU attach failures and a growing provisioning backlog. attach-fail rate +28% over baseline. logs show high fsync wait on /scratch.
raj: which pools / node groups are hot? any host IDs?
lucy: affected pools: scratchpool-aps1-a, scratchpool-aps1-b. example host gnode-aps1-043 (nvme0): util 95% io_qdepth 512, iowait up. attach queue length -> 120 pending.
nana: ops-bot alerted at 02:10: "attach-backlog: ap-southeast1 > threshold" btw the nightly janitor scrub kicked off 02:00 for hot-stripe compaction.
ops-bot: ALERT: attach-backlog.ap-southeast1 severity=warning count=3id. link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/attach-backlog/1714319876
maria: looks like janitor's full-scan cadence overlapped with a batch-scheduling wave. we should throttle scrub concurrency for scratchpool-aps1-* immediately.
dan: agree. short fix: reduce janitor concurrency and mark the worst nodes no-scrub so they stop extra io. quick commands: ```# reduce concurrency
kubectl -n janitor set env deploy/janitor JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=8 --overwrite
# label noisy nodes
kubectl label node gnode-aps1-043 redwood/no-scrub=true```
raj: can we cordon/reschedule GPUs off the noisy hosts so customers don't hit errors?
lucy: cordoning done for 3 hosts (gnode-aps1-043/047/054). rescheduling in progress, watching attach backlog.
maria: note the tradeoff: delaying scrubs increases wear backlog/cost later but keeps provision latency down. for now target-only noisy hosts, then run low-priority catch-up on cold nodes overnight.
dan: also consider temporary qdisc/qdepth change on nvme devices to smooth bursts, but that needs kernel patch window — not for immediate.
raj: cost question — if we throttle scrubs for 12 hours what's estimated added background work? rough estimate ~+12% extra scrub hours on weekend, tooling team?
maria: rough calc: shift -> +3 node-days of scrub work per cluster, minor. cheaper than customer SLA hits.
lucy: action items: 1) reduce janitor concurrency (done) 2) label/suppress scrubs on noisy hosts (done) 3) cordon/reschedule GPUs (in progress) 4) follow-up: schedule catch-up jobs on cold cohort overnight and add telemetry to correlate janitor window vs attach failures. I'll post a short postmortem if this reappears.
nana: thumbs up :thumbsup: keep us posted if backlog clears or if attach fails spike again.
ops-bot: NOTE: runbook link for attach-backlog mitigation: https://runbooks.redwood/attach-backlog
